reason: The text contains several regular (non-royal, non-military leadership) characters who demonstrate agency and make meaningful choices. Most notably, the woman of Tekoa (from chapters 14) is brought to David by Joab and independently uses wisdom and persuasive rhetoric to influence the king's decision regarding Absalom. She asks questions, makes arguments, and drives forward the plot through her own initiative. Additionally, Shimei son of Gera demonstrates agency by choosing to curse and stone David; messengers like Achimaaz and Jonathan make decisions about their actions; and servants and subordinates make their own choices within their roles. These characters are not merely passive recipients of others' decisions but active participants who shape events.
